title: Cache coordination for continuous batching and prefix-linearizability
creator: Ava Chen
description: Problem statement: Continuous batching in the serving runtime introduces variable lifetime and ordering semantics for KV cache entries. When many inflight requests are coalesced into batches, the KV cache can be exposed to spikes of allocation and eviction pressure that interact poorly with simple LRU or TTL heuristics, and with prefix-scoped access patterns. This ticket scopes a correctness-first design and implementation that ensures prefix-linearizability (a practical consistency target for our prefix-key caching), safe eviction under continuous batching, and measurable GPU memory behavior. The goal is not only to avoid correctness regressions, but to provide provable invariants that are testable by unit, integration, and fuzz tests.
background: Context: Recent customer incidents showed rare but reproducible mis-serves when large batched requests caused transient KV cache churn. Existing eviction heuristics (LRU, TTL) work in steady-state, but they lack composition guarantees when batches merge, split, or when prefix-aware access causes interdependent churn across tenants. We also observe out-of-memory tail events on GPUs when prefetches combined with batching allocate overlapping prefix entries. Prior work in the repo targets eviction atomicity and prefix-awareness, but none address continuous-batching semantics or per-batch ghost accounting used by the allocator.
proposed_solution: Summary: Implement a hybrid eviction composer with three coordinated subsystems: (1) batch-scoped reference leasing, (2) ghost-footprint accounting for speculative prefetch/pipeline allocations, and (3) a prefix-affinity eviction arbiter that enforces prefix-linearizability. Details: - Batch-scoped leases: every serving batch obtains a lightweight lease token tied to the batch lifetime. When a batch reads/writes KV entries, the entries are tagged with the active lease token(s). Eviction will not reclaim entries referenced by any active lease. This prevents premature eviction during in-flight continuous batches without blocking normal LRU heuristics for idle entries. - Ghost footprint accounting: speculative allocations (prefetch, warmup caches) increment a ghost counter by prefix. Ghost counters throttle speculative prefetches when the prefix's ghost+resident footprint approaches a soft quota. Ghosts age with TTL similar to entries but do not block eviction permanently. - Prefix-affinity arbiter: eviction policy composes LRU and TTL with a prefix affinity score. When eviction candidates are chosen, candidates that would break prefix-linearizability (i.e., cause an apparent reorder or missing prefix history for an in-flight or shortly following request) are deprioritized. The arbiter enforces three invariants: (A) no eviction that would invalidate any active lease; (B) total GPU allocated bytes stay below configured watermark with hysteresis; (C) eviction decisions are monotonic per-prefix within an epoch to simplify reasoning. Implementation notes: use a lock-free lease table with epoch stamps to avoid global locks; piggyback lease checks on the allocator's free path. Tests will include deterministic schedule replay, property-based fuzzing for batch merge/split, and a GPU-memory stress harness that reproduces the incident pattern.
acceptance_criteria: Unit tests covering lease token lifecycle (acquire, renew, release) and eviction rejection while lease active
Integration test: batch merge scenario where two batches reference overlapping prefixes and eviction does not cause served outputs to change order or content
Fuzzing harness that runs 1M randomized batch sequences and asserts prefix-linearizability invariant holds
End-to-end GPU stress test reproducing prior tail OOM pattern reduced below threshold on staging cluster
Documentation added to runtime/kv_cache/README.md describing the lease model, ghost accounting, and tuning knobs
Benchmarked latency and throughput impact <= 3% p50 change for representative prompt mixes
rollout_plan: Canary rollout: 5% of traffic on dedicated pools with synthetic workloads for 48h
If stable, expand to 25% for 72h while monitoring memory and error budgets
Full rollout to runtime-1.22 after signoff from SRE and Performance
Fallback: graceful disable of lease gating which reverts to existing LRU/TTL behavior
monitoring: Dashboard: KV Cache Safety -> Lease hold count, lease contention rate, ghost footprint per-prefix
Telemetry: instrument per-eviction decision tag (reason: LRU/TTL/prefix-affinity/lease-blocked)
SLO check: eviction-induced miss-rate regression < 0.5% over 24h rolling window
risks: Lease tokens add metadata — increased memory for metadata in high-concurrency tenants
Ghost counters may delay beneficial prefetches if soft quotas set too conservatively
Complexity in allocator codepath could introduce latencies if not implemented lock-free
Incorrect epoch handling can allow stale lease acceptance; mitigations include defensive checks and epoch bumps on cluster upgrades
